research_question: What do the FTC's 2025 fraud and Consumer Sentinel figures measure, and what do they leave out?

research_brief.purpose: Report FTC fraud loss and Consumer Sentinel figures and explain their scope.
research_brief.audience: Consumers and writers looking for sourced identity theft and fraud figures.
research_brief.scope_limitations: Figures are reports made to the FTC, not total incidence. The sources checked give no separate 2025 count of identity theft reports. United States only.

statistics.claim: About $16 billion in fraud losses was reported to the FTC in 2025, the highest on record and about 25% more than 2024.

People reported losing $3.5 billion to imposter scams in 2025; nearly one in three fraud reports were about imposter scams; nearly $1 billion was lost to business impersonators and about $920 million to government impersonators.
More than 9.2 million fraud, identity theft, financial, and Do Not Call reports were added to the Consumer Sentinel Network in fiscal 2025; nearly 2,400 law enforcement users have access.
statistics.population: Reports to the Consumer Sentinel Network
statistics.limitations: A count of reports across four categories, not identity theft cases

content_gaps: Ranking pages quote FTC counts without saying they are voluntary reports.
Fraud losses and identity theft reports are often blended.
Several pages come from identity protection sellers.
Partial-year counts are presented as annual totals.
value_add: A scope-first reading of the FTC figures: what a report is, what the totals include, and what they cannot show.
